name: Sidestep
text: Quick. Next to the creature's aim: its next hit misses. On its aim: it skips its turn.
engine_cost: none
motif: footwork: ghost trails, footprints, dust
changes_play: Turns the shown aim into a target.

name: Old Saying
text: Gives {a} to your linked piece that fires next. With an environment piece in the chain, {b} more.
engine_cost: none
motif: scroll unfurls, ink words fly into the linked piece
changes_play: Rewards chaining through weather.

name: Loaded Die
text: Roll 50% + 2% per Luck point (max 90%). On a hit the piece it links to fires twice, on a miss once.
engine_cost: small: shared Luck roll condition and a refire action
motif: lid opens, cell-shaded cube spins out and lands on the piece
changes_play: Placement picks which piece gets doubled.

name: Sharp Eye
text: Keeper. Held: you see the piece the creature plays after its aim. Played: its next piece loses {a}.
engine_cost: small: show the creature plan next piece while held
motif: eyelid, vision cone, crack
changes_play: Foresight you can spend.

name: Skitter
text: Evade: the creature's next Hurt misses, and the piece that missed tumbles off the board.
engine_cost: none: existing clauses evade and @miss kill (the miss phase carries the creature piece id, as block does).
motif: Edges as scuffed footprints; fire: the gnome skitters sideways and the creature's piece skids off the edge.
changes_play: You choose when to let a big Hurt come; the miss costs the creature a board piece, not just a hit.
risk: Strong against bosses' 3-fire pieces. Guard rail: only the one Hurt that misses; a boss piece loses one firing instead of falling.
worth_it: A dodge that also clears the board: the missed Hurt cannot fire again or anchor the creature's next chain.

name: Wrong Turn
text: Quick. The creature's aim moves one cell, to the free cell next to it farthest from its own pieces; if its piece does not fit there, it must pick again.
engine_cost: small: new action 'shove' moves foe.plan x/y to a free neighbour (pfb_foe_plan already re-aims when a cell is bad); the aim chip recomputes via pfb_aim_total.
motif: Edges as a crooked signpost; fire: the aim marker gets spun like a weathervane and hops one cell over.
changes_play: You steer where its next piece lands: away from its links and into your setup (or off the cell you need).
risk: Can strand the creature over and over. Guard rail: once per round; a bird's second aim is not moved.
worth_it: Taking the aim cell today only makes it re-pick its best move; Wrong Turn moves its committed move to a worse cell of your making.

name: Pinning Stance
text: Hold. While it stands, if the creature has to pick again it may only pick a cell touching this piece; if none fits, it loses that move.
engine_cost: small: pfb_search for the creature's re-pick filters cells to the stance's neighbours while one of yours stands.
motif: Edges as planted boots; fire: the gnome stamps, and a pin pops into the aim marker and drags it close.
changes_play: The aim cell becomes a lever: take it, and the creature's piece is pulled beside your stance (or wasted).
risk: Lock with Long Hop each turn. Guard rail: at most one lost move per round; the lost piece goes back to its hand, not to waste.
worth_it: Today a blocked aim just re-picks a move as strong as the old one; Pinning Stance makes the re-pick land where you want it, into your guard and your Riposte.

name: Shadow Step
text: Keeper. When the creature places its aimed piece, this jumps from your hand onto a free cell touching it and fires there.
engine_cost: medium: a reaction hook after the creature's pfb_place; picks the fitting cell with most of your links. Keeper is the existing @hand keep.
motif: Edges as a dark outline; fire: a shadow pours off the gnome and pops up beside the creature's piece.
changes_play: You plan around its aim: the guard goes up right as its piece arrives, and your piece now sits in its chain's way.
risk: A free extra placement each round. Guard rail: it fires alone (no chain) and only if it fits; once a round, then it is used up.
worth_it: A placement on the creature's turn: you answer its move the moment it lands.

name: Phantom Footing
text: Evade. For the next two rounds you choose where the creature's aimed piece lands: any free cell next to its aim where it fits.
engine_cost: medium: an aim-redirect pick in the player's turn stored on foe.plan, honoured by the creature's placement.
motif: Edges as misty footprints; fire: the gnome fades, and a ghostly hand slides the creature's aim marker.
changes_play: The creature's plan becomes your placement: you build both sides of the board.
risk: Can strand every creature piece. Guard rail: two rounds, one cell from its aim, only where it fits; if none fits it plays its aim.
worth_it: Total control of where its pieces go for two rounds: next to nothing, or into your Riposte setup.

name: Knot of Twine
text: Its four sides fit and link any knob or hole, whatever the family (a flat side or a Mud still does not link). The piece it links to gets +{b}.
engine_cost: small: a new edge kind 'any' in pfb_joint (links with knob or hole of any family, fits but does not link with flat); authored edges on the tile (pfb_v1_tile already takes 'edges'). The boost is the existing boost clause.
motif: Edges are loose twine loops that tighten onto whatever knob or hole they touch; on fire the twine cinches and a small knot glows on the linked piece.
changes_play: You place it where two or three pieces of different families meet and turn them into one long chain (into a weather piece, through your old pieces); that is a different act from the free flip, which only swaps a piece's top and bottom and never changes a family.
risk: Linking on every side also pulls in touching creature pieces, which fire for the creature in your chain; rail: it is never a combo partner, flats and Mud stay unlinked, and the lit-spot numbers already show the health it would cost.
worth_it: The only piece of yours that links across families on all four sides, so a hand that matches nothing on the board still makes a chain, and it can be the hub that ties two chains into one.

name: Lantern Chain
text: Every other piece of yours in its chain gets +{b}. If the chain has 4 or more pieces, they get +{a} instead.
engine_cost: small: new action 'boostall:N' (loops the chain like ctype and adds wv to your pieces not yet fired); clen exists.
motif: Edge is a strung paper lantern; on fire a line of little lanterns lights piece by piece down the whole chain.
changes_play: Pushes you to build wide chains of 4+ instead of firing small pairs, and to place it in the middle of a long line.
value: v = 2 + stat/5; each other piece +{b}, +{a} in a chain of 4+
risk: Stacks with Sun into burst turns, and a boost stays on a board piece (wv) for its later firings; rail: added before Sun, at most +{a} per piece per chain, your pieces only (a 3+ chain uses them up anyway).
worth_it: The chain-builder's reward: one piece lifts the whole chain, not just the one it touches.

name: Weather Lore
text: When it fires, the environment's next piece becomes a Sun (a Spring on large boards), and it comes in on a free cell beside Weather Lore if there is one.
engine_cost: medium: rewrite $s['env']['next'][0] to the sun / spring tile from pfb_env_table(), and give pfb_env_place a preferred cell next to the Lore piece (its fit check pfb_env_fit exists).
motif: Edge is a weathervane cockerel; on fire it spins, clouds part, and the face-up environment card flips to a bright sun.
changes_play: You set up next turn's double-value chain on purpose, choosing where Weather Lore goes so the Sun arrives in your line instead of a far corner.
risk: Too much Sun, and the creature can link the Sun first; rail: once a round, the field cap (envmax) still applies (the Sun waits as now), and the creature moves before the environment places, so it can answer.
worth_it: You call the weather you need and where it lands: next turn a Sun sits right next to your pieces, ready to double a chain.

name: Copybook
text: The piece it links to learns the tag of another piece of yours in its chain (Pierce, Poison, Hold, Bash...) and keeps it for the rest of the fight, even after it is discarded.
engine_cost: small: write 'tag' onto the target board tile (pfb_discard already carries the tile to your discard, so the tag stays with that piece for the fight); a capped counter in $s['me'].
motif: Edge is a ruled copybook line; on fire the source piece's tag icon is traced in pencil and inked onto the linked piece.
changes_play: You plan which tag to teach which piece; a fight now has a deck that grows smarter round by round.
risk: Teaching Heavy or Quick onto everything; rail: one taught tag per piece, a taught tag never replaces an existing one, at most {b} pieces taught per fight.
worth_it: Permanently improves your deck mid-fight: a plain Swing comes back as a Pierce Swing every time it is drawn.

name: Turn of the Tale
text: The creature piece it links to becomes yours where it stands: it keeps its number and edges and fires for you in this chain and after.
engine_cost: medium: set the board piece's 'by' to 'me' and mark it stolen (pfb_discard sends it back to the creature, pfb_fire_lim keeps its budget); the aim is recomputed by pfb_intent as now; the JS twin tools/pfengine.js needs the same.
motif: Edge is a storybook page mid-turn; on fire the page turns over the creature piece and it re-inks in your colours, edges unchanged.
changes_play: You aim to link to its best Hurt; the creature loses its plan and you gain a piece that was never in your deck.
risk: Stealing boss anchors, and your pieces have no fire budget so a stolen piece would never wear out; rail: once a fight, not in boss fights, it keeps the creature's fire budget, and when it leaves it goes to the creature's discard (never your deck).
worth_it: The capstone of rewriting the board: the creature's strongest piece now hits for you.

name: Hedge Rummage
text: Placed: Pluck with your Luck roll (50% + 2% per point, max 90%, halved against a great creature) instead of Pluck's small chance. If it misses, the creature's next Hurt gets +{b}.
engine_cost: small: the shared Luck roll (new pfb_wx_cond 'roll' = pf_rand < min(90, 50 + 2*Luck)%, rolled once per firing and cached in cx so 'roll' and '!roll' agree; not in the code yet, Loaded Die needs it too); a pluck mode 'roll' in the existing pluck action, and a creature next-Hurt bonus (the mirror of fnext, which only shrinks).
motif: Edge: a blue knob with a sprig of hedge. Fire: a small hand rummages in a hedge, comes out with a glint (hit) or a bramble scratch that flies at the creature (miss).
changes_play: A real gamble: you pick a calm round to rummage, since a miss feeds its next hit and a missed Pluck can be tried again.
risk: Loot faucet; rail: still lifts one item a fight, halved on great creatures, rolls only when placed (refiring in a chain does not Pluck again).
worth_it: Pluck tops out at 35% by Luck 9; this is the only Pluck that keeps getting better with Luck, at a price.

name: Long Shot
text: Roll. Hit: it fires twice. Miss: the next Hurt you place gets +{a}.
engine_cost: small: the shared Luck roll (one new pfb_wx_cond 'roll' = pf_rand < min(90, 50 + 2*Luck)%, rolled once per firing and cached in cx so 'roll' and '!roll' clauses agree); 'again' reuses Loaded Die's fire-twice code for the piece itself; next:hurt exists.
motif: Edge: a long thin arrow nock on the knob. Fire: a pebble arcs far off screen, then (hit) a second pebble follows it in.
changes_play: Rewards building a Hurt-heavy follow-up; a self-contained double unlike Loaded Die's linked double.
risk: Double damage spikes; rail: low base value, doubles only itself, not the chain.
worth_it: A Hurt that doubles itself most of the time and banks its miss into your next swing.

name: Magpie's Pinch
text: Roll. Hit: take the creature's strongest hand piece; it is one of your next hand's 5 pieces, as yours. Miss: take its weakest hand piece instead.
engine_cost: medium: move a foe hand piece into your next hand, re-owned (by = me, value rescaled).
motif: Edge: a black-and-white feather on the knob. Fire: a magpie swoops across the board and carries a tile to the hand tray.
changes_play: Opens play with creature pieces (their edges, their types) in your own hand.
risk: Stealing a boss Hurt; rail: on a boss it rolls twice and needs both; a stolen piece fires at your values and is gone after use.
worth_it: Always robs the creature: usually its big move, at worst its filler, and you get a strange piece to play.

name: Turn of the Coin
text: Roll. Hit: the creature's strongest hand piece goes back into its draw pile and it draws another. Miss: it still loses {b} from that piece.
engine_cost: small: swap one foe hand piece with its draw pile, then re-plan (pfb_intent).
motif: Edge: a coin set on edge in the blue knob. Fire: a big coin spins above the creature and its strongest hand tile spins away into its pile.
changes_play: Lets you answer a scary round by reshuffling the creature's hand, not by guarding.
risk: Erasing boss signature moves; rail: a boss's ability pieces cannot be sent back, only shrunk.
worth_it: Rerolls the creature's worst threat: bad luck becomes its problem.

name: Lucky Streak
text: Roll until you miss (at most {b} times). Each hit: a random piece of yours on the board fires again.
engine_cost: medium: a loop of rolls that refires random own pieces through the existing fire path.
motif: Edge: a row of lit bulbs along the body knob. Fire: lights chase around the board, each lit tile flashes and fires.
changes_play: Rewards keeping many of your own pieces out; different from Loaded Die (random board pieces, not a link).
risk: Runaway refires; rail: at most {b}, a piece refires at most once, it never refires itself or other Luck pieces.
worth_it: Turns a full board into a slot machine: up to {b} extra firings, any type.

name: Soft Spot
text: Pierce. If the creature has guard up, it loses {a} guard. Your next Hurt this fight gets +{b}.
engine_cost: none (pierce tag, fguard fstrip:a, next:hurt:1:b).
motif: Edge: a small chalk X on the knob. Fire: a chalk circle draws on the creature's bark and cracks it.
changes_play: Guard-heavy creatures become a two-beat rhythm: mark, then strike.
value: v = 2 + stat/10; a = 1 + stat/5; b = ceil(a/2)
risk: Stacks with other Pierce pieces; guard rail: the strip needs guard up, the bonus is one Hurt only.
worth_it: Marks a weak spot: the guard a creature built on its turn (it stays through yours) is broken now and the next Hurt is set up.

name: Not Fooled
text: Guard. The creature's next chain gets no combos: no Ambush, Bait or Riposte for it.
engine_cost: small: a foe flag 'nocombo' that skips pfb_set_combo for who = foe, cleared at the end of its turn.
motif: Edge: a raised eyebrow arc. Fire: the creature's combo label appears, then is crossed out with a shake of the head.
changes_play: You read 'combo Ambush' on the aim chip and answer it, instead of only blocking the hit.
risk: Dead against creatures that never combo; guard rail: one chain only, its piece values are untouched.
worth_it: Creature chains get combos from the whole chain, and the aim chip names the combo it is about to land; this cancels exactly that.

name: Saw It Coming
text: Hold. Each creature Hurt this guard blocks is knocked off the board and its next piece loses {a}.
engine_cost: none (hold tag, @block kill, @block fnext:a).
motif: Edge: a small open eye on the shield rim. Fire: the eye blinks as the hit lands and the creature tile shatters.
changes_play: Rewards guarding against the shown aim; it thins the pieces its later chains need.
risk: A long-held guard removing every hit; guard rail: the cut is a max, removal only on a real block.
worth_it: Guarding where you know it will strike cleans its board and blunts its follow-up.

name: Snare Field
text: Up to {b} empty cells next to it become snares for 2 rounds; a creature piece placed on one loses half its value. The creature cannot see them.
engine_cost: medium: a snare mark per cell (like the ground map pfb_ter) and a halve on creature place.
motif: Edge: a coiled loop of twine. Fire: little loops spring from the piece to its neighbouring cells and glint.
changes_play: You fence the board around the shown aim; your read of its layout decides the fight.
value: v = 1 + stat/10; a = 1 + stat/5; b = ceil(a/2)
risk: Too much denial on 3x3; guard rail: max {b} cells, 2 rounds, the creature's search ignores them (it cannot see them).
worth_it: Area denial plus a big cut; if its committed aim cell becomes a snare, the aim still lands there.

name: Eyes of the Wood
text: Keeper. Held: you see the creature's whole hand and the piece it draws next, and every piece it aims loses {a}.
engine_cost: medium: send foe hand and draw top in pfb_view while held; set foe wnx a at each pfb_intent.
motif: Edge: leaf eyes along the border. Fire: eyes open among the board's leaves and the creature's hand fans out face up.
changes_play: You stop guessing: every round is solved against its real options; the cost is a hand place each round.
risk: Information aura is very strong; guard rail: only while held (Keeper), the cut is the aimed piece only.
worth_it: Its hand is the one thing the game hides; seeing it plus a steady cut on every committed move is total foresight.
